summary: filesystem_plugin.cpp:1659-1665 and :1734-1744. VERIFIED by the security reviewer and re-run by the orchestrator on libc++/macOS with the plugin flags: one regex_match over a 48-byte name takes 1 ms at depth 3, 15 ms at depth 4, 142 ms at depth 5, 1355 ms at depth 6 (about 9x per level), no regex_error is thrown so regex_gave_up never fires, and the deadline and shutdown cancel are polled only between entries. libc++ keeps its complexity counter per sub-match and __lookahead::__exec starts a fresh counter (read from the SDK header by the C++ reviewer); a 254-byte name with a depth-4 pattern takes 6.4 s. Linux: libstdc++ _M_lookahead builds a fresh sub-executor per evaluation so the cost is polynomial with degree equal to the nesting depth (likely; read in 16.2.0, CI uses gcc-15); Windows speculative. Blast radius (cpp-safety): command pool is clamp(cores,4,32) workers with a 1000-deep queue and no per-action cap; ~ThreadPool joins every worker with no deadline in scope on every Subscribe-stream end (agent.cpp:4008), so one pinned worker blocks reconnect and shutdown. Independent reporters: security-guardian only (Gate 2 wave); the C++, platform, plugin and compliance reviewers corroborated after being shown it. FIX (the orchestrator routes it through the Architect): refuse a lookahead opened inside another lookahead (paren-stack scan, keeps ^(?!.*\.bak$).*\.log$) or refuse any (? other than (?:, as a pure function in filesystem_search_dir.hpp with fixture cases; correct the comment at :1661/:1741, README.md:24-25, t2_capabilities.yaml:40-45 (and the regex parameter text), upgrading.md:16 (an operator-visible refusal must be named) and the changelog fragment, then regenerate the README fences and content/plugin-docs/filesystem.json; TEST: one file named 48 x "a", pattern (?=.*(?=.*(?=.*x))) (depth 3, 19 bytes), regex=true, match_type=files, assert rc 1 and the exact refusal row, captured RED before the fix; never run depth >= 5; search and replace share the heuristic (see sec-2-sibling-actions-unescaped-names-and-regex-class).

trigger: A Windows directory holds two entries whose names differ only in which UTF-16 unit is unpaired, for example a<U+D800>b.txt and a<U+DC00>b.txt, or one of them beside a real a<U+FFFD>b.txt; search_dir with a pattern that matches them (find_by_hash too, when both files hash to the target) returns the same path text on every one of those rows.
classification_rationale: A later review round turns the earlier error row (the whole walk ended) into a reported entry: path_utf8 now hands the shared converter (agents/shared/win_str.hpp from_wide, WideCharToMultiByte without the invalid-character flag) the name's UTF-16 units, and every unpaired unit, high or low, becomes the same three bytes, U+FFFD. The PR's own unit case pins both halves (test_filesystem_search_dir.cpp:519, an unpaired high unit, and :520, an unpaired low unit, each expect the same bytes a<U+FFFD>), so two such names, or one beside a real U+FFFD name, produce identical result rows: the operator cannot tell them apart, the count is right, and a follow-up action that takes the reported path as UTF-8 addresses a different file or none. Same class as the open UP-9-distinct-names-one-row (the POSIX and CR/LF/backslash folds), reached on Windows by a new mechanism. The rendering is disclosed (README.md:27, upgrading.md:18, the changelog fragment), and the 'can read alike' sentences (t2_capabilities.yaml:69, upgrading.md:18) name only CR, LF, invalid bytes and a trailing backslash, so the Windows case is absent from them: not a contradiction, no required doc absent, hence not filed as a documentation finding. Rare trigger (a name with an unpaired unit is made by faulty software or on purpose), rendering is the owner's disclosed choice, no wrong count and no data loss: I8 with E3 and E5 derives LOW. likely, not verified: the Windows leg owns the converter's runtime behaviour; a re-statement of the documented conversion, run on macOS over the name shapes, shows the collision. Fold into the UP-9 follow-up: add the Windows case to the same sentences.
